subject: Urgent: brief maintenance window to apply safety patch
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:23-07:00
Subject: Brief model drift detected — preliminary analysis

Hey Lauren,

We observed a short window (approx 6–9 minutes) of elevated generation latency and higher perplexity on a subset of customer requests routed to the 8xA dedicated pool after the 02:00 UTC rollout. Preliminary traces point to a KV cache alignment issue when the new kernel selection path was used in mixed-quant runs.

Impact: ~0.5% of active requests saw additional token latency and a small increase in trailing-token re-generation (visible in logs as KV-miss/reroute). No data corruption observed; all requests completed successfully or were rerouted.

We have a small compatible patch that forces a conservative cache-index validation before using the new path. Patch ready to deploy as a hotfix; estimated application time: 20–30 minutes per region with a brief (<5 min) rolling traffic shift. I attached the diff and a short safety checklist.

Attachment: kv_cache_alignment.patch.diff (text) — contains the guard check and fallback
Attachment: safety-rollforward-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Recommend: we notify affected customers with a short advisory and start the hotfix now to avoid recurrence. If you want, Marcus can run the rollout and I will monitor telemetry.

Stephanie
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Ops <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: brief maintenance window to apply safety patch

Hi Acme team —

We just detected a brief service anomaly affecting a small percentage of requests in the US region. To prevent any recurrence we will apply a targeted hotfix to validate KV cache indices for the new execution path. The patch is non-disruptive in data terms but requires a short rolling maintenance in your routed region.

Planned action: apply hotfix immediately with a 20–30 minute rolling window in US region. Traffic will be shifted to healthy nodes for <5 minutes during each rack swap. We do not expect request loss or data changes; all customer data continues to be isolated and retained per your contract.

What we are asking: please acknowledge receipt of this notice. If you have a tight SLA window now, tell us and we'll coordinate a narrower swap window.

We will post live updates on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-06-14-kv-alignment

Thanks — we'll confirm when the rollout completes.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme-corp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T10:12:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: brief maintenance window to apply safety patch

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the heads up. We just got a few 500s around 08:58 UTC and saw slightly degraded response quality for ~10 minutes. Appreciate the quick action.

Two quick questions:
1) Any chance this will affect message ordering or logs we rely on for debugging? We need to keep our event audit for compliance.
2) If this recurs, what are the remediation/credit steps under our contract?

If helpful I can loop in our Platform lead; otherwise ack'ed — go ahead with the hotfix.

— Jane
Platform Ops, Acme Corp
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T16:02:11-07:00
Subject: Postmortem notes: hotfix applied and next steps

Team —

Summary: we deployed kv_cache_alignment.patch across the US dedicated pools at ~10:05 UTC; rollout completed by 10:30 UTC. Customer-observed 500s around 08:58 UTC were correlated with the transient KV-miss path activation during the rollout of the kernel selection optimization. No data loss or ordering changes were detected; logs/audit entries preserved.

Actions taken:
- Stephanie applied the guard and ran a conservative rollout (completed 10:05–10:30 UTC).
- Marcus validated API-level telemetry and request counts; no retention anomalies.
- Aditya prepared a backfill verification job to scan for re-generated tokens across affected request IDs (job scheduled for 16:30 UTC).

Follow-ups:
- Engineering: add an invariant test to the kernel selector (PR opened, will land after code freeze window) — owner: Stephanie.
- Product: review the customer-facing postmortem for Acme and adjust SLAs language if needed — owner: Lauren.
- Sales/Support: prepare credit guidance template if customers request SLA credit — owner: Marcus.

We'll publish a concise customer postmortem to Acme by EOD and post the internal writeup to the incident folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExamplePostmortem

Thanks all for the quick coordination.

— Lauren
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
